statements.text: I'm a UX designer at a fintech startup called Paisabridge, two years in now.
Currently staying in a PG in Koramangala, Bengaluru. Shared kitchen and all, it's chaos.
I'm vegetarian, always have been. Mum would disown me otherwise.
My phone is a OnePlus 9 and the battery is basically dead.
My little brother Rohan just started engineering at NIT Trichy.
Karthik is my manager at work. Super hands-off, which I love.
Mornings start with two cups of ginger chai, no sugar. Non-negotiable.
Had masala dosa with Meera at MTR on Sunday, the queue was totally worth it.
Moved out of the PG! Got my own 1BHK in HSR Layout now.
Picked up a Pixel 8a last weekend, the camera is unreal.
Adopted a tabby kitten called Biscuit, the flat finally feels lived in.
The HSR place has a tiny balcony where I'm trying to grow basil and mint.
I do a Cult.fit HIIT class three mornings a week.
I'm allergic to peanuts, found out the hard way at a wedding buffet.
Biscuit seemed lonely so a grey cat called Pepper has joined the household.
Last day at Paisabridge today. Starting Monday as senior product designer at Lumen Health!
My new manager at Lumen is Neha, ex-Google, very structured.
Lumen's office is out in Whitefield so I'm doing Uber Pool both ways, nearly an hour each way.
Doctor flagged low B12, so I've started eating eggs and fish. Not strictly vegetarian any more.
Dropped the HIIT classes and took up running instead. Training for the Bengaluru 10K.
Turns out I'm lactose intolerant too, so it's oat milk for me from now on.
Neha moved over to the platform team. Samir Rao is my manager now.
Whitefield commute sorted. Purple Line metro plus a short feeder bus, about 45 minutes.
My friend Meera is a designer at Swiggy now.
Swapped the morning chai for South Indian filter coffee, chai just doesn't do it for me any more.

statements.text: I teach physics and maths at Bergen Katedralskole, going on twenty years now.
We live in a house in Fana, about 25 minutes south of Bergen.
I drive an old Volvo V70, diesel, and I love it far too much to sell.
Four cups of black filter coffee a day. My wife says it's a problem.
We have a Norwegian elkhound called Loke, thirteen years old and moving like a retired boxer.
Every Sunday morning I walk up Ulriken, whatever the weather.
My daughter Sigrid is studying marine biology in Tromsø.
I'm still on my iPhone SE from 2020, the battery sags in the cold.
The Volvo's a 2011 model, dark blue, with 290,000 km on the clock.
The doctor put me on amlodipine for my blood pressure, one tablet each morning.
I play cello in an amateur orchestra, rehearsals on Wednesday evenings.
Doctor says I have to cut the coffee down to two cups a day.
Sold the Volvo to a neighbour's son and now I'm driving a used Tesla Model 3.
Spent the weekend in Oslo with my wife; we finally saw the Munch museum.
I've also joined a choir, so it's cello and singing every week now.
My son Eirik works for Equinor in Stavanger, two weeks on and two off.
After a palpitations scare last week it's decaf only from now on.
We've moved into a flat in Nordnes; the house in Fana was too much to maintain.
The vet says Loke needs glucosamine every day for his joints.
My doctor swapped the amlodipine for losartan, it's kinder on my ankles.
Finally upgraded to an iPhone 15 Pro and the battery no longer dies when it snows.
I've accepted a lecturer post at the Western Norway University of Applied Sciences; my last day at the school was Friday.
Knee operation went fine, but the surgeon banned hiking, so I swim at Nordnesbadet instead.
Swapped the Tesla for a Skoda Enyaq, we needed a bigger boot for the cello.

statements.text: I'm an ER nurse at Hospital Civil here in Guadalajara.
Right now I'm on night shifts, three a week, 8pm to 8am.
We have a dog called Canela. Chihuahua mix, very dramatic.
I drive a 2016 Nissan March, silver, it has survived everything.
Trying keto at the moment: no tortillas, which is basically a crime in Mexico.
My husband Luis teaches maths at a high school in Tlaquepaque.
We rent a two-bedroom house in Colonia Providencia and the landlord is lovely.
My phone is a Samsung Galaxy A32 with a crack right across the screen.
I take English classes on Tuesday nights, I'd love to work abroad someday.
It's about 35 minutes by car to the hospital, and parking there is a nightmare.
Mateo plays for a little youth club on Saturdays, he thinks he's the next Chicharito.
Gave up keto, I missed tortillas too much. Eating normally again, just less sugar.
My tutor is Ms Harper, she's from Leeds and keeps correcting my 'th' sounds.
Took the kids to Lake Chapala on Sunday and Mateo fell in with his shoes on.
Finally on day shifts, 7am to 3pm. Sleeping like a human again.
Bought a pair of goldfish for the kids, Tortilla and Taco. Canela is suspicious.
Showed the kids photos on my new iPhone 13 mini and now they won't give it back.
Started a Friday Pilates class with my friend Ana, it's killing me.
My English class has moved to Thursday nights now that my shifts are settled.
Christmas Eve shift is done, tamales with the whole family tonight.
Just finished my first week as ER charge nurse at Hospital Angeles, after eleven years at Hospital Civil.
Mateo quit football and swims on Saturdays now, says the water is quieter.
Hospital Angeles is close enough that I cycle there, ten minutes door to door.
My cousin Beto sold me his Mazda 3 for a fair price, it drives so smoothly after the March.
Got the keys to our own house in Zapopan today!

statements.text: I'm doing a master's in urban planning at U of T, started last September.
I rent a room in a shared flat in Kensington Market, three of us in total.
I pull shifts as a barista at Roast & Row on College Street.
My phone's an iPhone 12 and the battery is toast, but I can't afford a new one.
I bike everywhere on an old Trek I got off Kijiji for 150 bucks.

I speak Ukrainian, Russian and English with family and friends.
I'm vegan, three years now. Toronto makes it easy.

Bouldering at the Bloc twice a week is the only thing keeping me sane during midterms.
Trek got stolen outside Robarts, so it's the TTC with a monthly pass for me now.
Had homemade pierogi at Taras's place on Saturday, first real ones in months.
Dr. Okafor's on sabbatical, so Dr. Haddad is supervising me now.

I'm allergic to shellfish, carry an EpiPen everywhere.
Started French classes on Wednesday evenings, because Canada.
Moved in with my girlfriend Priya near Dundas West. Finally out of the shared flat.
Quit the cafe. I'm a research assistant in the planning department now, mostly interviewing cyclists.
My thesis is on bike lane equity in the suburbs, 40 interviews done so far.
Wrecked my wrist bouldering, so I've given it up and swim at the Athletic Centre instead.
Cancelled the TTC pass, bought a used Brompton off a guy in Parkdale.
Caved and started eating eggs and cheese again, vegan life plus thesis stress was too much.
Dr. Haddad took a job in Vancouver, so Dr. Lindqvist is taking me on.
Also turns out I'm allergic to penicillin, found out at urgent care.
Also started using Zotero for citations, it's saving my thesis.

statements.text: I retired from Leeds Central Library three years ago, after thirty-one years on the issue desk.
I live in a little terraced house in Headingley with a postage-stamp garden.
My cat Marmalade is fourteen and has opinions about everything.
Yorkshire Tea, strong, with a splash of milk, six cups a day. Don't tell my doctor.
I read everything on my old Kindle Paperwhite now, paperback print is getting far too small.
My daughter Philippa teaches at a primary school in Ilkley.
I take atorvastatin every night for my cholesterol.
I sing alto in the Headingley Community Choir, Thursday evenings at seven.
I drive a 2012 Honda Jazz, red. It only ever does the supermarket and the garden centre.
I also help out at the Oxfam bookshop on Tuesday afternoons.
I've got an allotment in Meanwood, plot 14, growing mostly beans and far too many courgettes.
Wednesday mornings I go out with the walking group, usually around Otley Chevin.
The doctor wants me off the caffeine, so it's decaf Yorkshire Tea now. It tastes of disappointment.
Marmalade is a ginger tom with one ear, lost in a scrap with a fox years ago.
Poppy and Alfie bought me a Kobo Clara for my birthday, the backlight is a godsend.
My brother Graham lives in Perth, Western Australia, and sends me photos of sunshine I resent.
Had fish and chips in Whitby with Margaret on Saturday, a seagull stole half my chips.
Hip replacement done and dusted. I've swapped the walking group for aqua aerobics at the leisure centre.
The cardiologist moved me onto rosuvastatin because the atorvastatin gave me aches.
Traded the Jazz in for a little electric Fiat 500, silent as a cat.
Brought a second cat home from the shelter, a tabby kitten called Pickle.
Moved into my bungalow in Harrogate on Friday. Boxes everywhere and no kettle.
Gave up the Meanwood plot and put raised beds in the new garden instead.
Joined the Harrogate Singers last night. Posher than Headingley, but better cake.
Failed my eye test for driving, so the Fiat's gone and I've got a bus pass now.

statements.text: I'm the sous chef at an izakaya called Tsubame in Namba.
I rent a tiny 1K in Tennoji, ten minutes' walk from the station.
I cycle to work, fifteen minutes along the canal, rain or shine.
My shiba inu Mochi is two years old and absolutely hates rain.
After closing most nights I have a couple of highballs. It's my ritual.
My younger brother Kenta is a pharmacist in Nagoya.
I play drums in a covers band, rehearsals Sunday afternoons in Shinsaibashi.
I'm still on my old iPhone SE, the one with the home button. I refuse to move on.
I speak Japanese and decent English, thanks to an exchange year in Vancouver.
Went fishing off Wakayama with Daiki on Sunday and caught eleven horse mackerel.
Doctor says my liver numbers are bad, so I've quit drinking completely.
I'm allergic to buckwheat, which is a funny problem for a Japanese chef.
I jog five kilometres around Tennoji Park every morning before prep.
Picked up a Pixel 9, the camera is brilliant for photographing plated dishes.
Discovered I'm allergic to kiwi too, found out at a New Year's party.
Started online Korean lessons twice a week, I'm obsessed with Seoul street food.
Adopted a rescue cat called Tofu, and Mochi is still sulking about it.
Left Tsubame at last: I'm head chef at a kaiseki restaurant called Hanaori in Kyoto.
Moved into a two-room place in Fushimi, Kyoto, with a real kitchen.
The walk to Hanaori takes twelve minutes, so the bike is gathering dust.
Quit the covers band when I moved, and now I'm in a jazz trio in Kyoto that rehearses on Saturday nights.
Now I jog along the Kamo river each morning, beats circling Tennoji Park.
Dropped the Pixel into a stockpot. Bought an iPhone 16 out of shame.
Hanaori only seats twelve people at the counter, so every plate is basically personal.

statements.text: Hi, I'm Nandini. I'm a product manager at a payments startup called Paynest, here in Hyderabad.
We're renting a two-bedroom flat in Gachibowli. Ten minutes from the office, and that alone justifies the rent.
My phone is still a OnePlus 9 and the battery is dead by 3pm every single day, ugh.
I've been vegetarian since I was a kid, so team lunches are always a negotiation.
Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings are yoga at the Rasa studio. Non-negotiable.
Filter coffee runs my life. Two cups before ten, no exceptions.
My husband Karthik is an architect at a small firm in Jubilee Hills.
We have a beagle called Biscuit who is three and has destroyed every pair of my slippers.
Found out I'm allergic to peanuts the hard way, at a cousin's wedding. Never again.
My brother Arjun works at Google in Dublin and keeps sending me photos of the rain.
Spotify is on all day while I work, mostly Telugu and Tamil film music.
Got a Pixel 9 last week, loving it. The camera is unreal.
Big change: I've joined Razorpay as a senior product manager, first day was Monday. Paynest is behind me.
We ate way too many bobbatlu at Karthik's parents' place for Ugadi, I think I gained a kilo.
At the new job I'm working on the merchant onboarding revamp, we're targeting a June launch.
Cancelled my Rasa membership. My mornings now belong to a running club, three days a week around the Gachibowli stadium.
We have a Maruti Swift but honestly it mostly just sits in the parking lot.
We bought a flat in Kokapet and moved in last weekend. No more landlord drama!
Doctor told me to up my protein, so eggs and fish are back on the menu. Not really vegetarian any more.
Biscuit has a new housemate, a tabby kitten we named Dosa.
Turns out I'm also allergic to shellfish. Learned that in Goa last week, the prawns were not worth it.
I'm also the PM for the refunds dashboard at Razorpay, that one's due in August.
By the way, the Swift is the red 2020 VXi.
Acidity got so bad the doctor made me stop coffee entirely. It's chamomile and ginger tea for me now.
We finally let go of the Swift and brought home a Hyundai Creta. Karthik chose the colour.
Sprained my ankle so the running streak is over, for now. I'm doing home yoga with YouTube videos instead.
Dropped Spotify for YouTube Music, it came free with my phone plan.

statements.text: I'm a nurse at Mater Hospital in Nairobi, maternity ward.
I rent a bedsit in Kasarani. It's tiny but my landlady, Mama Joy, is wonderful.
Getting to work is a matatu and then a boda boda, about ninety minutes each way when it rains.
My phone's a Tecno Spark 10 with the screen cracked in two corners, but it still does M-Pesa so I'm not complaining.
I send my mum in Nyeri 5,000 shillings every month towards her rent.
Saving up for a plot in Kitengela, a little bit set aside every payday.
This quarter it's night shifts for me, 7pm to 7am, three nights a week. My sleep schedule is in ruins.
Chai with loads of ginger keeps me alive, three cups a day at least.
Saturday at 7am is netball with the hospital team, I never miss it.
My little brother Kevin is doing mechanical engineering at the University of Nairobi.
Finally got a Samsung Galaxy A35 last week. The old Tecno gave up completely.
I've started a diploma in critical care nursing at KMTC, classes every other Sunday.
Moved to a one-bedroom in Roysambu! A real bedroom door, a bit of privacy.
Back on day shifts from Monday, 7 to 4. My body is so grateful.
My cat Simba has decided the new bed is his and I'm just visiting.
My knee finally gave up on netball so now I swim on Saturday mornings at the Kasarani pool.
Transferred to Aga Khan University Hospital. Same maternity work, better pay.
Started baking banana bread on my days off. The first loaf was a brick.
Mum's landlord raised her rent, so it's 8,000 shillings a month from me now.
Had nyama choma with my cousin Achieng on Sunday, she's tired of living in Buruburu.
I'm fostering a tiny tortoiseshell kitten called Zuri until she finds a home.
Swapped chai for black coffee, my colleague got me hooked on the machine at the nurses' station.
Achieng and I took a two-bedroom in Parklands, so I walk to work now. Goodbye matatus!
Paid the deposit on the Kitengela plot today! Months of saving finally paid off.
Passed my first critical care exam with a B and cried in the corridor.

statements.text: I'm the sous chef at Bistrô Marcelo, four years in and I still love the chaos of Friday service.
We live in a third-floor apartment in Batel and the lift breaks every other week.
My daughter Lara is seven and has decided she will only eat pasta. A chef's kid, can you imagine.
I'm Coritiba till I die, season ticket holder since 2012.
I drive an old Fiat Uno, 2008, no air conditioning, and I'm weirdly attached to it.
CrossFit at the box near the market, five mornings a week before I head to the kitchen.
Our mutt Pipoca is half labrador and the vet says she needs to lose two kilos. Too many kitchen scraps, my fault.
I've got a Moto G 5G. The camera is good enough to photograph plates.
Cafezinho with two sugars, I know, I know.
My dad is an Athletico Paranaense fan, so Sunday lunches are always tense.
Spent a long weekend in Floripa with Camila and ate the best oysters of my life.
Bought a used iPhone 13 from a colleague, still figuring out where everything is.
Doctor put me on losartan for my blood pressure, one pill every morning.
Big news, I'm head chef at Casa Pinhão starting Monday. Four years in Marcelo's kitchen are done.
My cafezinho is black now. Camila shamed me into it.
Our son Theo arrived on the 12th, 3.4 kilos, mom and baby are both fine and nobody is sleeping.
With a newborn CrossFit is dead to me. I jog around Parque Barigui when I can steal an hour.
I've started brewing beer at home, the first batch is an American pale ale.
We signed the lease on a house in Santa Felicidade today, goodbye elevator!
The Uno is the red four-door, in case you wondered, and the rust is winning.
At Casa Pinhão I'm building the winter menu, the tasting is on 10 July.
I'm also responsible for the Sunday brunch menu there, which launches on 2 August.
Sold the Uno at last and bought a Hyundai HB20. Air conditioning, finally!
The doctor swapped my blood pressure pills for amlodipine, the losartan was giving me a cough.
We adopted a beagle puppy called Feijão, and Pipoca is not amused.
My knee quit on the jogging so I've switched to cycling with a Saturday group instead.
Watched Coritiba beat Paraná two nil at the Couto Pereira last Sunday. The whole stand was shaking.

statements.text: I'm in my second year of the chemical engineering master's at Chalmers.
I've got a room in a student corridor in Johanneberg, kitchen shared with eleven other people. Chaos.
To afford rent I work Saturdays at a café on Linnégatan, mostly pouring oat lattes.
I cycle everywhere, even in sleet. The bike is a beat-up old Crescent that I love far too much.
Been vegan for about two years now.
My laptop is a 2020 MacBook Air and it wheezes whenever I open Aspen Plus.

My phone is an iPhone 12 with a cracked back that I keep meaning to fix.

My thesis is due on 30 June, and the draft is very much a draft.
I'm learning Spanish on the side because I'm going to Chile in July.
Gave up on veganism, I eat fish and eggs again. I got anaemic and my doctor wasn't subtle about it.
Moved into a two-room flat in Majorna with my friend Oskar.
My Crescent got stolen last week, so I'm on trams with a monthly pass now.
Swapped the iPhone for a Fairphone 5, I wanted something I can actually repair.

Apparently kiwis make my mouth itch too, the allergist says it's related.
Back from Chile, Valparaíso was my favourite and I ate far too many empanadas.
I volunteer at a school STEM club on Wednesday afternoons.
I've moved my bouldering membership to a hall in Mölndal, it's cheaper.
I've stopped working at the department, it's thesis only until I hand it in.

statements.text: I'm a primary school teacher at Scarborough Primary in Perth. Twenty-two years and counting.
My class this year is Year 4, twenty-six kids and one very loud classroom hamster.
I rent a little villa in Doubleview. The landlord won't let me paint a single wall.
I drive a Mazda 3, it's a trusty old thing.
Chloe, my daughter, is in her second year of vet science at Murdoch.
Since the divorce it's me and my ginger cat Gizmo, who rules the house.
I swim laps at the Scarborough pool at 6am, three mornings a week, before school.
My phone is an iPhone SE from 2020, small but it does the job.
I'm a tea person. A pot of Earl Grey every morning, and don't talk to me before.
I'm in a book club that meets on the first Thursday of the month, we're deep into Tim Winton at the moment.
My sister Narelle is a nurse at Royal Perth Hospital, she works nights.
Blood test says I'm low in iron, so I'm taking a tablet every morning.
The Mazda is a 2012 hatch in white, and the aircon only works on a good day.
Started pottery on Wednesday nights at a studio in Fremantle. My first bowl looks like a hat.
The pool's closed for the rest of the year, so I run along the beach path now instead.
They've moved me up to Year 6 this term. Fewer hamsters, more attitude.
Dropped the SE in the ocean, so I'm on a second-hand iPhone 13 now.
I bought a two-bedroom unit in Innaloo! Settlement's done and the keys are in my hand.
Gizmo has competition. I adopted a grey boy from the RSPCA called Pavlova and Gizmo is not impressed.
Off Earl Grey for a month now, it's rooibos with honey in the mornings.
New school, new title: I'm deputy principal at Karrinyup Primary from Monday. Last day at Scarborough was a tearful one.
The Mazda finally died on the Mitchell Freeway, so I bought a used Toyota Corolla hatch.
Iron's back to normal, the doctor says I can stop the tablets.
Chloe's home for the break and cooked a lamb roast. She burned the potatoes, I said nothing.
My son Jack's FIFO roster in Karratha is two weeks on, one off, and he's already bought a ute.
We read Cloudstreet for book club this month and I cried at the end.
I'm planning to walk the whole Bibbulmun Track next April, all one thousand kilometres.

Doc has me on metformin, twice a day, for the sugar.
My phone is a Jitterbug flip phone. My granddaughter Emma keeps trying to drag me into the smartphone age.
Spent the whole weekend in the garage on a cherry bookcase for Dolores. Woodworking is my thing.
Been working my way through every Louis L'Amour paperback at the library sale.
Duke, our yellow Lab, is ten now and his hips are shot.
My son Greg is a pharmacist in Columbus.
Folgers, black. I'll hear no complaints about my coffee.
Took Dolores to Olive Garden for our forty-second anniversary. She ordered the same thing she always does.
Blood pressure's up so it's low sodium everything now. Food has no taste.
Emma finally won: I'm on an iPhone SE now and texting like a teenager.
Tuesday mornings I volunteer at the food pantry at St. Mark's.
I sing bass in the St. Mark's choir, rehearsal is Wednesday nights.
Traded the old Ford for a used 2019 Chevy Silverado. Sad to see the F-150 go, but my knees can't take the step up anymore.
Got the left knee replaced yesterday at OhioHealth. Walker for six weeks.
My hands aren't steady enough for the saw any more, so it's watercolours for me now. Dolores says my barn looks like a cow.
Duke's on glucosamine chews for those hips and the vet says he's doing better.
They switched me off metformin and onto Jardiance.
Doctor wants me off caffeine, so it's decaf Folgers from here on out.
Sold the Maple Street house and we're now in a condo in Sarasota, near Dolores's sister. Had to give up the food pantry and the choir too, and that stings.
Joined the pickleball bunch at the condo, Monday and Wednesday mornings. I'm terrible.
We took in a little terrier mix named Pepper, and Duke acts like he owns her.
Cardiologist says my pressure's fine, so the salt shaker is back on the table.
Greg and his wife Priya are expecting twins in January.
Sold the Silverado, condo parking is tight. We're a one-car household now, a Buick Encore.
Dolores gave me an Apple Watch for my birthday, it nags me when I sit too long.
